Declare onevcs maintenance for idle warm-pool slots using `cargo-prune-superseded` 0.1.1, installed by bootstrap. Cleanup removes superseded Cargo builds older than two days while preserving each unit’s newest build and all recent builds.

Superseded build output across the host’s pool reached about 926 GB and nearly filled a 1.8 TB disk twice in four days. Repository-owned cleanup reclaims obsolete output while keeping builds warm. The budget bounds how long regular maintenance holds a slot out of service.

The only dependency change in `Cargo.lock` is `rustls` 0.23.45 → 0.23.46, addressing the advisories reported by the required deny check (RUSTSEC-2026-0346 through RUSTSEC-2026-0349). The incidental change to `tempfile`’s `getrandom` dependency was reverted; no other locked dependency moves.

body:
## What

Consolidate macOS CI and release work to at most one Mac job per workflow run and two Mac-spending runs per change lifecycle, while preserving Linux/Windows coverage and protected check names. **Intel macOS artifacts are discontinued from the next release; macOS distributions now support Apple Silicon only.**

## Why

The five-runner macOS pool is shared across repositories. Repeated platform jobs let one change occupy several scarce slots, delaying otherwise green work and dependent releases. Consolidating the existing checks and builds frees capacity for other changes.

## Additional info

### Scheduling and required checks

Ordinary affected PRs run Mac cross-platform checks and installed-binary proofs sequentially in one job. Linux carriers retain the exact `cross (macos-latest)` and `install (macos-latest)` display names. They run with `always()`, reject failed, cancelled or missing prerequisites, and explicitly report when Mac work was legitimately omitted. Existing Linux/Windows checks and path-sensitive skips remain.

The shared semantic classifier permits release-only omission only for a same-repository release-plz branch whose parsed diff contains exclusively version/changelog changes. Author identity and PR title grant no exemption. Fork-headed release branches, mixed changes, same-named registry dependency changes, unreadable PR input and unrecognised event names require the Mac lane. Package source distinguishes repository packages from registry dependencies.

The following figures compare baseline `2b0eb1ee0d95924010226d4bd0ee0d78a9098bd6` with the finished workflow graph. Release routes are **contract-level evidence, not observed release executions**.

| Workflow | All declared triggers | Before: maximum Mac jobs/run | After: Mac jobs/run |
| --- | --- | ---: | --- |
| `ci.yml` | push to main; pull_request opened, synchronize, reopened | 2 (`cross (macos-latest)`, `install (macos-latest)`; Apple Silicon) | Ordinary affected PR: 1; release-only PR and base pushes: 0 |
| `release.yml` | release published | 11 (6 Apple Silicon + 5 Intel, broken down below) | 1, building and proving Apple Silicon artifacts before publication |
| `published-smoke.yml` | workflow_run completed for Release; workflow_dispatch | 4 (2 Apple Silicon `macos-latest` + 2 Intel `macos-15-intel`) | Automatic/default manual: 0; explicit manual diagnostic: 1 (Apple Silicon) |
| `visual-docs.yml`, including pinned screencomp v0.4.8 reusable workflow | pull_request opened, synchronize, reopened, closed; push to main; workflow_dispatch; monthly schedule | 0 | 0 |
| `release-plz.yml` | push to main | 0 | 0 |
| `notignored.yml` | pull_request | 0 | 0 |

Baseline Mac job rows by target, read from `2b0eb1ee` (the Intel rows are **removed** in the after graph, so Intel macOS artifacts are discontinued):

| Workflow / job | Apple Silicon (`aarch64-apple-darwin`) before | Intel (`x86_64-apple-darwin`) before | After |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `release.yml` / `upload` | 1 (`macos-latest`) | 1 (`macos-latest`, cross-target) — **removed** | folded into the one Apple Silicon `macos` release job |
| `release.yml` / `verify-assets` | 1 (`macos-latest`) | — | folded into the one Apple Silicon job |
| `release.yml` / `build-wheels` | 1 (`macos-latest`) | 1 (`macos-latest`, cross-target) — **removed** | folded into the one Apple Silicon job |
| `release.yml` / `verify-pypi` | 1 (`macos-latest`) | 1 (`macos-15-intel`) — **removed** | folded into the one Apple Silicon job |
| `release.yml` / `build-npm` | 1 (`macos-latest`) | 1 (`macos-latest`, cross-target) — **removed** | folded into the one Apple Silicon job |
| `release.yml` / `verify-npm` | 1 (`macos-latest`) | 1 (`macos-15-intel`) — **removed** | folded into the one Apple Silicon job |
| `published-smoke.yml` / `pypi` | 1 (`macos-latest`) | 1 (`macos-15-intel`) — **removed** | 0 automatic; Apple Silicon only in the opted-in diagnostic |
| `published-smoke.yml` / `npm` | 1 (`macos-latest`) | 1 (`macos-15-intel`) — **removed** | 0 automatic; Apple Silicon only in the opted-in diagnostic |

Tag pushes and repository_dispatch trigger no workflow here. The modeled automatic lifecycle spends Mac time in one ordinary PR run and one release run: **two runs total**. Base pushes, release-only PRs and their merges, downstream smoke and schedules spend none. The default-off manual diagnostic is outside that lifecycle.

### Distribution and migration notes

**Intel macOS archives, wheels and the `onepipeline-api-cli-darwin-x64` npm carrier stop shipping with the next release.** Previously published versions remain available. The npm launcher now refuses Intel macOS with “Intel macOS is no longer supported” instead of attempting to resolve a missing carrier; a packaging test covers that refusal. The Darwin builder also rejects the discontinued target before compilation.

| Retained Rust target | Release archive | PyPI carrier | npm carrier |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu` | `.tar.gz` + `.sha256` | `onepipeline-api-cli` wheel | `onepipeline-api-cli-linux-x64` |
| `aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu` | `.tar.gz` + `.sha256` | `onepipeline-api-cli` wheel | `onepipeline-api-cli-linux-arm64` |
| `x86_64-pc-windows-msvc` | `.zip` + `.sha256` | `onepipeline-api-cli` wheel | `onepipeline-api-cli-win32-x64` |
| `aarch64-apple-darwin` | `.tar.gz` + `.sha256` | `onepipeline-api-cli` wheel | `onepipeline-api-cli-darwin-arm64` |

All other released platforms and artifact types remain. The crates.io `onepipeline-ui` crate, npm `onepipeline-api-cli` launcher and npm `onepipeline-ui` frontend remain published under their existing names.

The Apple Silicon release job compiles once with maturin, then derives archive and npm payloads from the final wheel binary. Hash comparisons enforce byte reuse. It installs and runs all three forms natively, including the server-and-embedded-browser proof, before Linux jobs upload or publish them. Checksums and the CycloneDX SBOM remain in the release path. No Rosetta or Intel cross-compilation step remains.

### Recorded verification

The implementation's recorded local results are for head `3d4a51ce19e06a5aa4d47fa49c7aa0caa2ec194e`; these checks were not rerun while preparing this description.

- `node --test .github/tests/*.test.mjs`: **25/25 passed**. Journeys cover generated git histories, classification and production routing, real workflow matrices and Actions expressions, reusable calls, event fan-out, protected names, carrier outcomes, unsupported-resolution errors and release declarations.
- The regression for the failure at `2d2aa06` passes under `GITHUB_REF_NAME=315/merge`. Release-command subprocesses strip inherited `GITHUB_*` state, so the external-toolchain failure case reaches its intended diagnostic instead of failing the release-tag check.
- `cargo test --test packaging`: **36/36 passed**, including the real host-native maturin build, archive/npm packing, pip/npm installs, server and embedded-view proof, byte-reuse checks and Intel launcher refusal. `cargo test --test e2e packaging::`: **5/5 passed**. Linux execution proves the host-native packaging path; Darwin compatibility is checked structurally here and executed natively by the release job.
- Workflow telemetry recorded **1,152 scenarios**, digest `405a4d2d…`. The two `macos-budget.mjs` reporters returned **1 job/run** and **2 runs/change**; `node .github/check-budgets.mjs` passed both bounds through the onebudgetspec SDK.
- `actionlint` over the three edited workflows, `node .github/lint.mjs`, `bash -n scripts/release-darwin.sh` and `git diff --check`: clean.
- `just lint-llm-diff origin/main`, against `45ac04670e1606c9c56fd9c61abbf2423e1ed09c`: **52 rules; 26 passed, 0 failed, 18 skipped, 8 not relevant**. Recorded history: `20261013T221759Z-917ab`.

Earlier sensitivity checks deliberately broke classification, carriers, routing, platform declarations and hashes; each induced regression failed its test and was restored. No release was cut.

The private `.github` tooling package shares the root lockfile. Its `github-workflows` Nx project joins affected selection and records telemetry through an uncached test target; budgets depend on that target and reject missing or stale telemetry. Production build journeys remain behind the packaging edge. The separate jobs/run budget catches one run occupying several shared Mac slots even when the lifecycle run count remains within its bound.

### Observed runs

These are observed GitHub states for [PR #315](https://github.com/nickderobertis/onepipeline-ui/pull/315), inspected at 2026-10-14T00:45Z. They are separate from the contract-level release routes above. Native Mac execution on this PR and a finished release execution are **not** claimed.

**Draft PR run (observed).** [CI 38476937779](https://github.com/nickderobertis/onepipeline-ui/actions/runs/38476937779) at head `3d4a51c`: changes, pr-title, llmlint, deny, msrv, browser-windows, `cross (windows-latest)`, both Linux `wheel` legs, `quality`, `gate`, `install (ubuntu-latest)` and `install (windows-latest)` succeeded, and `sweep` was skipped. The single `macos` job was **still queued** ~2h after `quality` finished at 22:46Z, behind three Release runs (v0.33.0, v0.34.0, v0.34.1) in the shared pool. Its `cross (macos-latest)` and `install (macos-latest)` carriers had therefore not reported. [Visual docs 38476938247](https://github.com/nickderobertis/onepipeline-ui/actions/runs/38476938247) succeeded with no Mac job; `report (x86_64, shots/current, shots/verify, Visual docs)` passed. [notignored 38476937851](https://github.com/nickderobertis/onepipeline-ui/actions/runs/38476937851) succeeded.

This PR was squash-merged as `a86ec83` at 2026-10-13T22:56:32Z with that `macos` job still queued.

**Post-merge base pushes (observed).** [CI 38481090578](https://github.com/nickderobertis/onepipeline-ui/actions/runs/38481090578) (`a86ec83`, this PR's base merge) and [CI 38488118758](https://github.com/nickderobertis/onepipeline-ui/actions/runs/38488118758) (`262b936`, the v0.34.1 release-PR merge) both **skipped** `macos`. In both, the `cross (macos-latest)`, `install (macos-latest)` and `gate` carriers succeeded as authorized omissions, so base pushes used **0 Mac jobs**.

**First release on the consolidated workflow (observed, in progress).** [Release 38488386121](https://github.com/nickderobertis/onepipeline-ui/actions/runs/38488386121) for v0.34.1 had `guard` succeeded and `test` in progress at inspection. It is not reported here as published.

**Earlier draft head (observed snapshot).** At `52a2314`, runs [38394418775](https://github.com/nickderobertis/onepipeline-ui/actions/runs/38394418775) and [38394419475](https://github.com/nickderobertis/onepipeline-ui/actions/runs/38394419475) were cancelled when the next commit superseded them. [notignored 38394418781](https://github.com/nickderobertis/onepipeline-ui/actions/runs/38394418781) succeeded.

The workflows deliberately keep `ready_for_review` out of their pull_request types, per #284, which `tests/e2e/ci_tier.rs` holds. Re-running on the lift would also spend a second Mac run for the same change. The earlier `checks-unsettled` publication result came from the draft run still being in progress, not from skipped runs.

### Suppression inventory

- `.github/fixtures/screencomp-v0.4.8.yml`: added file-level `comments_earn_their_place` suppression preserves verbatim upstream prose. Blob verification removes only that annotation, and a subprocess test rejects other upstream-byte changes. The snapshot also retains upstream's `changed_behavior_has_e2e` suppression: the reusable workflow forwards external repository/token values, while dedicated journeys cover the underlying maintenance behavior and contract tests cover wiring.
- `.github/workflows/release.yml`, `test` job: retains the existing `no_second_broader_sweep_over_an_already_gated_commit` suppression unchanged. A manually created Release can name a commit no earlier sweep covered, so this publication path still requires its own gate.
- `.github/budgets.yaml`: both registrations carry the approved separate-bound rationale as plain comments. The llmlint marker was omitted because `budgets_track_product_owner_outcomes` is not configured here. The jobs/run description also records the inner-measure reason.

The branch does not incorporate the later SDK bump at `45ac046`; that change touches no file edited by this branch.

## What

Relink the reader to onepipeline 0.70.0, pin onevcs to 0.48.1, and align the onetaskgraph libraries at 0.6.0 so the reader and engine share one version of each. Browser reply validation accepts the engine’s `rework` and `retitle` commands through typed JSON, and its event-kind corpus matches the linked libraries. The composer keeps its existing shortcuts.
